hero.title: Click. Install. Make music.
hero.description: The full StemTube audio engine — stems, chords, beats, lyrics, mixer — packaged as a single 1.4 MB Windows installer. The engine downloads itself on first launch. After that, everything runs offline on your machine.
hero.meta: v2.0.0 · 1.4 MB installer · Windows 10/11 x64 · ~3-8 GB after first-launch download
features.label: Features
features.title: What StemTube Desktop does
features.subtitle: Local-first audio analysis. Upload your own files, run everything on your own machine. No account, no telemetry, no internet required after install.
feature.stems.title: AI Stem Separation
feature.stems.desc: Split any song into vocals, bass, drums, guitar, piano and "other" using Demucs htdemucs_6s. NVIDIA GPU acceleration with CUDA, automatic CPU fallback.
feature.chords.title: Chord Detection
feature.chords.desc: Hybrid BTC Transformer + madmom CRF pipeline detecting 170 chord types. Real-time chord display with guitar diagrams synchronized to playback.
feature.beats.title: Beat Tracking
feature.beats.desc: madmom CNN + DBN downbeat detection. Detects beats and bar positions (1/2/3/4). Tap-sync to nudge the grid manually if needed.
feature.lyrics.title: Lyrics Transcription
feature.lyrics.desc: faster-whisper with word-level timestamps and karaoke-style highlighting. Dedicated Focus mode for distraction-free practice.
feature.mixer.title: Full Mixer
feature.mixer.desc: Per-stem volume, pan, mute and solo. Tempo adjustment with pitch correction (SoundTouch). Waveform with playhead scrubbing.
feature.privacy.title: Local & Private
feature.privacy.desc: Single-user, no account, no telemetry. Audio files never leave your machine. After first-launch download, the app works fully offline.
howItWorks.label: How It Works
howItWorks.title: From installer to mixer in three steps
step1.title: Install (1.4 MB)
step1.desc: Download the installer and run it. On first launch, the app fetches its 0.5-2.9 GB engine (Python + PyTorch + CUDA + Demucs + madmom + Whisper) from GitHub. Once. After that, launches are instant.
step2.title: Upload a track
step2.desc: Drop any MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A or other audio file. Demucs separates stems, BTC + madmom detect chords and beats, Whisper transcribes lyrics. All in parallel, all local.
step3.title: Mix and practice
step3.desc: Open the mixer: mute the guitar and play along with chord diagrams in real time, slow down the tempo without changing pitch, switch to karaoke focus to learn the lyrics.

crossPromo.server.label: Need more than one user, or mobile access?
crossPromo.server.title: There's a self-hosted server edition
crossPromo.server.desc: Same audio engine, plus: multi-user with per-account libraries, mobile PWA on iOS and Android, real-time jam sessions, shared global library, optional YouTube import. Runs on Linux, Windows or macOS — Python 3.12 setup script included.
story.label: About
story.title: A side project that grew up
story.p1: StemTube started as a vibe-coding experiment — what happens when you let AI-assisted development guide the process without a rigid plan? What was meant to be a weekend hack turned into a full music workstation.
story.p2: The Server edition (self-hosted, multi-user, mobile PWA, jam sessions) is the original. This Desktop edition packages the same engine for people who just want to double-click an installer and have it work. No Python knowledge required, no network setup, no account.
story.quote: After 25 years in IT, I wanted to give back to the open-source ecosystem that gave me so much throughout my career. StemTube is that contribution — imperfect, evolving, and open to everyone.
story.p3: Everything is open source — the Tauri shell, the Python backend, the audio pipeline. No tracking, no account required, no cloud dependency. Your music, your machine.
cta.title: Ready to try it?
cta.desc: Download the installer, double-click, wait for the engine to download on first launch, and start mixing.
disclaimer.title: Unsigned installer
disclaimer.desc: The installer is not signed with a Windows code-signing certificate (paid yearly subscription). Windows SmartScreen will display a warning on first launch. Click "More info" then "Run anyway". The installer and the engine zip are both hosted publicly on GitHub Releases for full transparency.

linux.title: Install on Linux
linux.desc: On Ubuntu/Debian, download the installer package and double-click it — like the Windows .exe. StemTube lands in your apps menu; the first launch detects your hardware and downloads the matching engine (CPU or NVIDIA GPU). On other distros, run the self-contained engine directly.
linux.appimage.title: Option A — AppImage (recommended)
linux.appimage.desc: One self-contained file with everything bundled — Python, PyTorch, FFmpeg. No dependencies, no Python version to worry about. Download, make it executable, run.
linux.appimage.note: The app opens in your browser. GPU version (~3 GB) comes in two parts — join them with cat. Needs libfuse2.
linux.script.title: Option B — install script
linux.script.desc: Clones the app and builds a Python environment from source. Prefer this if you want a system-wide install. Requires git and python3 (3.10–3.13 — not 3.14 yet, PyTorch has no wheel for it).
linux.script.note: Then launch with stemtube, or from your applications menu. The script detects your GPU and installs the matching PyTorch automatically.
linux.req: 64-bit Linux (glibc 2.35+) · NVIDIA GPU optional (CUDA accelerated), otherwise CPU. Needs an AVX-capable CPU — run it on real hardware; a VM that masks AVX will fail (PyTorch requires it).
linux.installer.title: Ubuntu / Debian — download & double-click
linux.installer.desc: An installer package — the Linux equivalent of the Windows .exe. Double-click it to install, then launch StemTube Desktop from your apps menu. The first launch detects your GPU and downloads the right self-contained engine.
linux.installer.note: Nothing else to install — the engine bundles Python, PyTorch and FFmpeg. It lives in your home folder; no system changes, no root at run time.
linux.manual.title: Other distros (Fedora, Arch, openSUSE…) — run the engine directly
linux.manual.desc: No package manager needed. Each engine is a single self-contained AppImage (Python, PyTorch, FFmpeg bundled) that runs on any 64-bit Linux.
linux.manual.note: --appimage-extract-and-run means no libfuse2 is needed. The GPU version (~3 GB) comes in two parts — join them with cat StemTube-x86_64-gpu.AppImage.part* > StemTube-x86_64-gpu.AppImage.
linux.fromsource: Developers: a from-source install script is also available (builds a Python env; requires Python 3.10–3.13).
linux.installer.step1: Install it: double-click the downloaded stemtube-desktop_2.1.0_amd64.deb. It opens in your software installer (e.g. App Center / Software Install) — click Install and enter your password. (Or in a terminal: sudo apt install ./stemtube-desktop_2.1.0_amd64.deb.)
linux.installer.step2: Launch it: open your applications menu, type “stem”, and click the StemTube Desktop icon.
linux.installer.step3: First launch downloads the engine. A small window appears while it fetches the matching engine — CPU ~600 MB or NVIDIA GPU ~3 GB. This is a one-time download and can take several minutes depending on your connection; the app window opens once it finishes. Later launches start in seconds.
